records.source: לַמְנַצֵּ֣חַ עַל־שֹׁ֭שַׁנִּים לִבְנֵי־קֹ֑רַח מַ֝שְׂכִּ֗יל שִׁ֣יר יְדִידֹֽת׃
records.gloss: For the director, on Shoshannim. Of the sons of Korah. A maskil. A song of loves.
pieces: For the music director. On shoshannim. Of the sons of Korah. A maskil. A love song.

L.1: For the director: on shoshannim. Of the sons of Korah. A maskil. A song of love.

R.1: For the leader of the music. To the tune "Lilies". By the family of Korah. A song to teach and give insight. A love song.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director
decisions.reason: As in 4:1.

decisions.choice: on shoshannim: "on lilies"
alternatives: to the tune of a song called Lilies
decisions.reason: The word means lilies (Song 2:16). It may name a tune, or an instrument; the musical sense is no longer known (69:1; 80:1).

decisions.choice: maskil
decisions.reason: As in 42:1.

decisions.choice: a song of loves: a wedding song for the king
decisions.reason: The psalm celebrates a royal wedding: the poet praises the king (verses 3-10), speaks to the bride (11-16) and promises the king lasting fame (17-18). Later readers, Jewish and Christian, also heard in it the Messiah, the coming king (Hebrews 1:8-9).

decisions.choice: to the tune "Lilies"; a song to teach and give insight
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likely sense (m2, m3).

records.heading: A wedding song for the king

records.source: רָ֘חַ֤שׁ לִבִּ֨י׀דָּ֘בָ֤ר ט֗וֹב אֹמֵ֣ר אָ֭נִי מַעֲשַׂ֣י לְמֶ֑לֶךְ לְ֝שׁוֹנִ֗י עֵ֤ט׀סוֹפֵ֬ר מָהִֽיר׃
records.gloss: My heart is stirred [with] a good word; I am speaking my works to [the] king; my tongue [is the] stylus of a skilled scribe.
pieces: A lovely theme has set my heart astir; I offer my verses to the king, and my tongue runs like the pen of an expert scribe.

L.2: My heart is stirred with a good word; I speak my works for the king; my tongue [is] the pen of a skilled scribe.

R.2: My heart is full of beautiful words. I am singing this song for the king. My words flow as fast as a skilled writer can write.

decisions.choice: is stirred: bubbles over
decisions.reason: The verb (rachash) occurs only here; it seems to mean to move or bubble up, like boiling water.

decisions.choice: I speak my works: the poet speaks of his poem
decisions.reason: Only here and in verse 18 does the poet speak of himself; "my works" are the verses he has made.

decisions.choice: the pen of a skilled scribe: words that come easily
decisions.reason: A skilled scribe (Ezra 7:6) writes quickly and well; so the poet's words flow.

records.source: יָפְיָפִ֡יתָ מִבְּנֵ֬י אָדָ֗ם ה֣וּצַק חֵ֭ן בְּשְׂפְתוֹתֶ֑יךָ עַל־כֵּ֤ן בֵּֽרַכְךָ֖ אֱלֹהִ֣ים לְעוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: You are fairer than [the] sons of man; grace is poured on your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever.
pieces: You are more handsome than anyone else; grace pours from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} lips; that is why God has blessed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forever.

L.3: You are fairer than the {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}}; grace has been poured on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} lips; therefore God has blessed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forever.

R.3: King, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are more handsome than any other man. You speak kind and gracious words. God has blessed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forever.

decisions.choice: you are fairer: very handsome
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled in form (yafyafita), which makes it strong: the king is beautiful beyond all others, as kings were praised to be (1 Samuel 16:12).

decisions.choice: grace poured on your lips: gracious, winning speech
decisions.reason: His words are pleasing and full of favor (Proverbs 22:11).

decisions.choice: therefore: the sign of God's blessing
decisions.reason: The words ('al ken) usually mean "therefore": his beauty and grace show that God has blessed him. They can also give the reason.

decisions.choice: children of humankind, with "sons of men" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As in 11:4.

decisions.choice: King,
decisions.reason: Readable names the one addressed.

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: The psalm addresses the king as "God" (verse 7), and Hebrews 1:8-9 applies verses 7-8 to Christ, so, as with the king in Psalm 2, the pronouns for the king throughout the address to him (verses 3-10 and 17-18) can be capitalized with the deity pronoun setting. The bride (verses 11-16) is not included.

records.gloss: Gird your sword on [the] thigh, mighty one, your splendor and your majesty.
pieces: Strap {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sword to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} side, mighty warrior, in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} splendor and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} majesty!

L.4: Strap {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sword on [{{deity_pronoun:your|Your}}] thigh, mighty one, [in] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} splendor and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} majesty.

R.4: Mighty king, put on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sword. Show how glorious and great {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are!

decisions.choice: sword on the thigh: ready for battle
decisions.reason: A sword hung at the hip from the belt (Judges 3:16).

decisions.choice: splendor and majesty: royal glory
decisions.reason: The words (hod, hadar) are often used of God's own glory (96:6; 104:1). God shares them with the king he has chosen (21:6).

decisions.choice: your splendor: the sword, or the king's array
alternatives: gird on your splendor and majesty
decisions.reason: The words stand without a verb; they may describe the king as he arms himself, or be more things he is to put on.

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

records.source: וַהֲדָ֬רְךָ֨׀צְלַ֬ח רְכַ֗ב עַֽל־דְּבַר־אֱ֭מֶת וְעַנְוָה־צֶ֑דֶק וְתוֹרְךָ֖ נוֹרָא֣וֹת יְמִינֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And your majesty, prosper, ride on for [the] cause of truth and humility [and] righteousness, and let it teach you awesome [things], your right hand.
pieces: In {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} majesty ride out to victory for the sake of truth, humility and justice; let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand show {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} deeds that inspire awe.

L.5: And [in] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} majesty ride on victorious for the cause of truth and humility [and] righteousness; and let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand teach {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} awesome [deeds].

R.5: Ride out in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} greatness and win! Fight for truth, for what is right, and for those who are humble. Your strong arm will do amazing things.

decisions.choice: prosper, ride: go out to victory
decisions.reason: The first verb (tsalach) is to succeed; with "ride" it means to ride on in triumph, as a king in his chariot.

decisions.choice: humility and righteousness
alternatives: the humble who are in the right
decisions.reason: The two words stand side by side without "and". They may name two causes, or "righteous humility". The king fights for what is true and right, not for himself.

decisions.choice: let your right hand teach you awesome deeds: your strength will show you great victories
decisions.reason: The king's own strength will lead him to deeds that fill others with awe.

decisions.choice: Your strong arm will do amazing things
alternatives: let your right hand teach you awesome deeds
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m3).

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

records.source: חִצֶּ֗יךָ שְׁנ֫וּנִ֥ים עַ֭מִּים תַּחְתֶּ֣יךָ יִפְּל֑וּ בְּ֝לֵ֗ב אוֹיְבֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: Your arrows [are] sharpened, peoples under you will fall, in [the] heart of the king's enemies.
pieces: Your arrows are sharp; peoples fall beneath {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; they pierce the hearts of the king's enemies.

L.6: Your arrows [are] sharpened — peoples fall under {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} — in the heart of the king's enemies.

R.6: Your arrows are sharp. They go deep into the hearts of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies, and nations fall down in front of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: arrows ... in the heart of the king's enemies: a broken line
decisions.reason: The middle phrase interrupts the picture: the arrows go into the enemies' hearts, and meanwhile peoples fall. The king is spoken of in the third person though he is addressed.

decisions.choice: they pierce (B); They go deep into (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the verb the picture implies (m1).

decisions.choice: your enemies
decisions.reason: Readable keeps speaking to the king.

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

records.source: כִּסְאֲךָ֣ אֱ֭לֹהִים עוֹלָ֣ם וָעֶ֑ד שֵׁ֥בֶט מִ֝ישֹׁ֗ר שֵׁ֣בֶט מַלְכוּתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Your throne, God, [is] forever and ever; a scepter of uprightness [is the] scepter of your kingdom.
pieces: Your throne, God, lasts for ever and ever; the scepter of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom is a scepter that rules rightly.

L.7: Your throne, God, [is] forever and ever; a scepter of uprightness [is] the scepter of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom.

R.7: God, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} throne will last forever. You rule {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom fairly.

decisions.choice: Your throne, God: the king addressed as God
decisions.reason: The plain reading is that the poet calls the king "God" ('elohim). Elsewhere the word is used of those who stand in God's place, such as Moses before Aaron (Exodus 4:16) or judges (82:6). Others read "your throne is God's" or "your divine throne". The ancient translations read it as an address, as Hebrews 1:8 does.

decisions.choice: Hebrews 1:8-9
decisions.reason: Hebrews quotes verses 7-8 as God speaking to the Son, to show that he is greater than the angels.

decisions.choice: a scepter of uprightness: just rule
decisions.reason: The scepter is the rod a king holds as the sign of his rule; a straight scepter means he rules justly (Isaiah 11:4-5).

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

records.source: אָהַ֣בְתָּ צֶּדֶק֮ וַתִּשְׂנָ֫א רֶ֥שַׁע עַל־כֵּ֤ן׀מְשָׁחֲךָ֡ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֱ֭לֹהֶיךָ שֶׁ֥מֶן שָׂשׂ֗וֹן מֵֽחֲבֵרֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you [with the] oil of joy above your companions.
pieces: You love justice and hate evil; that is why God, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} God, has anointed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, rather than {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} companions, with the oil of gladness.

L.8: You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} God, has anointed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [with the] oil of gladness above {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} companions.

R.8: You love what is right and hate what is evil. So God, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} God, has chosen {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} over all the others and poured oil on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} head. He has filled {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with joy.

decisions.choice: anointed with the oil of joy: chosen and honored
decisions.reason: Kings were anointed with oil when they were made king (1 Samuel 16:13). Oil was also poured on guests at a feast, a sign of joy (23:5); at his wedding the king is honored above all.

decisions.choice: God, your God: or "God, your God" addressing the king again
alternatives: therefore, God, your God has anointed you
decisions.reason: "God" may be the subject, said twice for emphasis, or the first "God" may again address the king, as in verse 7. Hebrews 1:9 reads it as an address.

decisions.choice: your companions: other kings, or the king's friends
decisions.reason: He is honored above all others of his rank.

decisions.choice: chosen you over all the others ... poured oil on your head
decisions.reason: Readable says what anointing meant (m1).

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

records.source: מֹר־וַאֲהָל֣וֹת קְ֭צִיעוֹת כָּל־בִּגְדֹתֶ֑יךָ מִֽן־הֵ֥יכְלֵי שֵׁ֝֗ן מִנִּ֥י שִׂמְּחֽוּךָ׃
records.gloss: Myrrh and aloes, cassia, [are] all your garments; from palaces of ivory strings make you glad.
pieces: Your robes all breathe out myrrh and aloes and cassia; the sound of strings from ivory-inlaid palaces brings {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} joy.

L.9: Myrrh and aloes [and] cassia [are] all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} garments; from palaces of ivory stringed instruments make {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} glad.

R.9: Your clothes smell of sweet perfumes. Music from palaces decorated with ivory makes {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} happy.

decisions.choice: myrrh, aloes, cassia: costly perfumes
decisions.reason: Myrrh is a fragrant resin, aloes a scented wood, and cassia a spice like cinnamon. All were rare and costly (Proverbs 7:17; Exodus 30:23-24).

decisions.choice: palaces of ivory: rooms inlaid with ivory
decisions.reason: Ivory was set into walls and furniture in the palaces of the rich (1 Kings 22:39; Amos 3:15).

decisions.choice: strings: stringed instruments
decisions.reason: The word (minni) is probably a form of the word for strings (150:4); it could also mean "from".

decisions.choice: sweet perfumes
decisions.reason: Readable names the kind of thing rather than each one.

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

records.source: בְּנ֣וֹת מְ֭לָכִים בְּיִקְּרוֹתֶ֑יךָ נִצְּבָ֥ה שֵׁגַ֥ל לִֽ֝ימִינְךָ֗ בְּכֶ֣תֶם אוֹפִֽיר׃
records.gloss: Daughters of kings [are] among your honored [women]; [the] queen stands at your right hand in gold of Ophir.
pieces: Princesses are among the ladies of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} court; at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand stands the queen, adorned with gold from Ophir.

L.10: Daughters of kings [are] among {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} honored women; the queen stands at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand in gold of Ophir.

R.10: Daughters of kings are among the women who serve {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Your bride, the queen, stands at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right side, wearing the finest gold.

decisions.choice: the queen: the king's bride
decisions.reason: The word (shegal) is a royal wife (Nehemiah 2:6). The bride of the wedding now stands in the place of honor.

decisions.choice: at your right hand; gold of Ophir
decisions.reason: The right hand is the place of honor (110:1). Ophir was a land known for the finest gold (1 Kings 9:28; Job 28:16).

decisions.choice: the finest gold
decisions.reason: Readable says what Ophir gold meant (m2).

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

records.source: שִׁמְעִי־בַ֣ת וּ֭רְאִי וְהַטִּ֣י אָזְנֵ֑ךְ וְשִׁכְחִ֥י עַ֝מֵּ֗ךְ וּבֵ֥ית אָבִֽיךְ׃
records.gloss: Listen, daughter, and see, and incline your ear, and forget your people and the house of your father,
pieces: Hear me, daughter, take note and listen closely: leave behind your own people and your family home,

L.11: Listen, daughter, and see, and incline your ear; and forget your people and your father's house,

R.11: Listen, my daughter, and pay attention. Forget your own people and your family.

decisions.choice: Listen, daughter: the poet speaks to the bride
decisions.reason: The poet now turns to the bride, addressing her as an older man would a young woman (Ruth 2:8).

decisions.choice: forget your people: begin a new life
decisions.reason: The bride came from another land (verse 13 mentions Tyre). She is to leave her old home behind and belong to the king's house (Genesis 2:24; Ruth 1:16).

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The sentence continues in verse 12, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: וְיִתְאָ֣ו הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ יָפְיֵ֑ךְ כִּי־ה֥וּא אֲ֝דֹנַ֗יִךְ וְהִשְׁתַּֽחֲוִי־לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: and the king will desire your beauty; for he [is] your lord, and bow down to him.
pieces: then the king will long for your beauty. He is your lord; bow down to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.12: and the king will desire your beauty; for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] your lord, so bow down to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.12: The king will love your beauty. He is now your master, so bow down to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with respect.

decisions.choice: your lord: your husband and king
decisions.reason: The word ('adon) is used of a husband (Genesis 18:12) and of a king; he is both.

decisions.choice: bow down: honor him
decisions.reason: Bowing was the sign of respect for a king (1 Kings 1:16).

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

records.gloss: And [the] daughter of Tyre with a gift, your face they will entreat, [the] rich of [the] people.
pieces: Tyre's daughter will come with a gift; the wealthiest of the people will try to win your favor.

L.13: And the daughter of Tyre [will come] with a gift; the rich of [the] people will seek your favor.

R.13: People from the rich city of Tyre will bring you gifts. Wealthy people will want you to be kind to them.

decisions.choice: the daughter of Tyre: the people of Tyre
decisions.reason: A city is often called "daughter" (9:15). Tyre was a rich trading city on the coast north of Israel. The words may also mean a princess of Tyre, perhaps the bride herself.

decisions.choice: entreat your face: seek your favor
decisions.reason: To entreat someone's face is to try to win their good will (Proverbs 19:6).

decisions.choice: will come, will bring
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb in the first half; the sense is that they come with gifts.

records.source: כָּל־כְּבוּדָּ֣ה בַת־מֶ֣לֶךְ פְּנִ֑ימָה מִֽמִּשְׁבְּצ֖וֹת זָהָ֣ב לְבוּשָֽׁהּ׃
records.gloss: All glorious [is the] daughter of a king within; of settings of gold [is] her clothing.
pieces: The princess waits within, all splendid; her gown is woven with gold.

L.14: All glorious [is the] king's daughter within; of settings of gold [is] her clothing.

R.14: The princess is in the palace, and she is beautiful. Her dress is made with threads of gold.

decisions.choice: within: in her room in the palace
decisions.reason: The word (penimah) means inside a building, here in her chamber before she is led out. It is not a statement about inner character.

decisions.choice: the king's daughter: the bride
decisions.reason: The bride is probably called a king's daughter because she is a princess by birth; she may also be called so as the new queen.

decisions.choice: settings of gold: gold woven or set into the cloth
decisions.reason: The word (mishbetsot) is used of the gold settings of the high priest's gems (Exodus 28:11).

records.source: לִרְקָמוֹת֮ תּוּבַ֪ל לַ֫מֶּ֥לֶךְ בְּתוּל֣וֹת אַ֭חֲרֶיהָ רֵעוֹתֶ֑יהָ מ֖וּבָא֣וֹת לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: In embroidered [garments] she is led to the king; virgins behind her, her companions, [are] brought to you.
pieces: In bright embroidered robes she is led to the king, with her maiden companions following, brought to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.15: In embroidered robes she is led to the king; virgins [are] behind her, her companions, being brought to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.15: Wearing her colorful dress, she is led to the king. Her young friends follow her as they come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, the king.

decisions.choice: embroidered: woven in many colors
decisions.reason: The word (riqmot) is cloth of many colors, worked with the needle (Judges 5:30).

decisions.choice: to you: to the king
decisions.reason: The poet turns again to the king; some read "to him" instead.

decisions.choice: virgins, her companions: the bride's attendants
decisions.reason: Young unmarried women went with the bride in the wedding procession.

decisions.choice: the king
decisions.reason: Readable says who "you" is (m2).

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

records.gloss: They are led with joy and rejoicing; they enter [the] palace of [the] king.
pieces: Amid joy and celebration they are escorted in, and they go into the king's palace.

L.16: They are led in with joy and rejoicing; they enter the palace of [the] king.

R.16: Everyone is full of joy as they are led in. They go into the king's palace.

decisions.choice: joy and rejoicing: the gladness of a wedding
decisions.reason: Two words for joy are joined, as at weddings (Jeremiah 33:11).

records.source: תַּ֣חַת אֲ֭בֹתֶיךָ יִהְי֣וּ בָנֶ֑יךָ תְּשִׁיתֵ֥מוֹ לְ֝שָׂרִ֗ים בְּכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: In place of your fathers will be your sons; you will make them princes in all the land.
pieces: Where {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fathers once stood, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sons will stand; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will set them up as princes over all the land.

L.17: In place of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fathers will be {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sons; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will make them princes in all the land.

R.17: King, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sons will rule after {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fathers ruled before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. You will make them leaders everywhere in the land.

decisions.choice: your fathers, your sons: the king addressed again
decisions.reason: The pronouns are masculine again: the poet speaks to the king and promises him heirs from the marriage, who will carry on the royal line.

decisions.choice: the land
decisions.reason: The word ('erets) can mean the land of Israel or the whole earth.

decisions.choice: King,; rule after you, as your fathers ruled before you
decisions.reason: Readable says who is addressed and what "in place of" means.

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.

records.source: אַזְכִּ֣ירָה שִׁ֭מְךָ בְּכָל־דֹּ֣ר וָדֹ֑ר עַל־כֵּ֥ן עַמִּ֥ים יְ֝הוֹדֻ֗ךָ לְעֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃
records.gloss: I will cause your name to be remembered in every generation and generation; therefore peoples will praise you forever and ever.
pieces: I will make {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name remembered from one generation to the next; so the nations will give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} thanks for all time.

L.18: I will make {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name remembered in every generation; therefore peoples will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forever and ever.

R.18: I will make sure that people remember {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name in every age. People from every nation will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forever.

decisions.choice: I will cause to be remembered: the poet's promise
decisions.reason: The "I" is most likely the poet of verse 2, whose song will keep the king's name alive. Some take it as God's promise.

decisions.choice: peoples will praise you: more than any king
decisions.reason: The verb (yadah) is usually used of praise to God. The words reach beyond any one king of David's line, which is why the psalm was read of the Messiah (Hebrews 1:8-9).

decisions.choice: pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 45:3.
